headline: India's Technology Development Board has agreed to put Rs 86 crore, half the cost of a Rs 172 crore programme, into moving four AI-discovered drug candidates from the company Peptris toward clinical trials.
score_reason: Pool 4 kept: the statement came out on 12 Oct 2026 and the article matches the headline; the drug candidates are still before human trials.
importance_line: A government development fund is financing a three-year push to take four AI-found drug candidates, aimed at muscle, nerve, cancer and hair conditions, toward human trials, which matters over the long run to patients with those conditions, to Indian drug research and to Peptris, but the candidates are still before clinical trials, the money is a debt-style financing rather than a grant, and the statement gives no sign yet that any of them works in people.
source: IANS, citing India's Ministry of Science and Technology
summary: IANS, the Indian news agency, reports that India's Technology Development Board, a government body under the Department of Science and Technology, has signed an agreement to provide Rs 86 crore (860 million rupees) to Peptris Technologies, a company that uses AI to find drug candidates, for a three-year programme called VIGOR with a total cost of Rs 172 crore, according to an official statement from the Ministry of Science and Technology on Monday 12 Oct 2026. The programme aims to move four candidates, for neuromuscular disorders and cancer, hair loss, nerve damage and Duchenne muscular dystrophy, from early lab-stage work to preparation for clinical trials (levels 4 to 6 on the technology readiness scale, which rates how mature a technology is), and the money comes as optionally convertible debt, a loan-style financing that can be converted into shares, with the work subject to regulatory and scientific requirements.
notes: Read in full via IANS (fulltext). IANS relays the ministry's official statement. The article does not say who funds the other half of the Rs 172 crore or when the agreement was signed.
